{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → `uSplitPlate` (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group)
{{% /callout %}}

Splits contour plates into replacement plates: the source plate is replaced after the outputs and assembly have been checked. This is separate from Split (which cuts in place).

**How to use:**

1.  Select the contour plates, then choose a reference and click **Apply**. With nothing selected you are asked to pick the plates first (middle-click to finish); the point or line is always asked last.
2.  Point uses the nearest plate edge to establish a perpendicular split line. Line and Line 2 points project the picked line onto the plate surface.
3.  The command repeats until <kbd>Esc</kbd>; Apply starts a new pick session.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Reference** | Point, Line or Line 2 points. A projected corner, or a line outside the plate, leaves the plate unchanged. |
| **Gap** | Signed separation: positive separates the new plates, zero meets at the reference, negative overlaps them. |
| **Assembly** | Add to assembly keeps the original assembly; when the source was its main plate, the first replacement becomes main. |

Unsupported attachments and cutter types are blocked before the source plate is deleted.

{{% callout type="warning" %}}
On a partial failure, inspect the reported state and use native Undo before retrying.
{{% /callout %}}

**More details:**

-   Gap is signed separation: positive separates the new plates, zero meets at the reference, negative overlaps them.
-   It creates replacement plates and deletes the source after output and assembly checks succeed.
